question: Adversarially verify the cat5 response body layouts for op=0x14 (gold balance) and the warehouse item-LIST reply(s) that fill CTX+0x1b8 (ops 0x3d and 0x03), independently re-derived from 0x157394's jump table; flag any invented or mis-offset field.
independent_finding: All in-scope Map layouts are independently reproduced byte-for-byte from disasm; zero invented or mis-offset fields. Then fo 0x576a0-b2 put_u8(5);put_u8(0x3f);put_bytes(TXBUF,12) with TXBUF[4]=CTX[0x308] -> AUTO-SENDS cat5 op0x3f; server must be ready for inbound 0x3f. Matches Map. Rows @p[6+i*21]: [0]=flag,[1..20]=item. Body=4+21*N. Tail CTX[0x38]==3 @0x575ca. Exact match. Rows @p[5+i*21]. Body=3+21*N (3-byte header, no 0x1a5 write). Tail fn_0x175b98(global[sl+0x4b0],7,1,1) @0x57da4. Exact match. Endianness: all multi-byte fields are raw memcpy then read via ldr/ldrh on the LE ARM target => LE (byte layout HIGH; LE label = standard target endianness, HIGH).
corrections: No offset is invented or mis-placed; two precision refinements only (do not change any stated offset): (1) 'N must be <=16' / 'N <=16' in ops 0x3d/0x03/0x3f is BUFFER CAPACITY (the client memsets exactly 16 flag bytes + 16x20 item array), NOT a client-enforced clamp -- there is no min(N,16) anywhere in these handlers, the loop bound is the raw wire count N=CTX[0x1a6], so N>16 overflows CTX. It is a SERVER OBLIGATION, not a wire-validated rule. Map's reason (16-slot array) is correct but the wording over-implies enforcement. (2) op 0x03 additionally carries its own clamp CTX[0x1a5]=min(N,CTX[0x1a5]) at fo 0x57c9e-0x57cce (N=CTX[0x1a6]=p[3..4] vs the RETAINED prior CTX[0x1a5], which op 0x03 never writes from wire) -- undocumented in the Map's op 0x03 entry; harmless omission since all op 0x03 layout offsets are correct.
